The compound is a para-disubstituted benzene (two aromatic 1H NMR signals) with an ester group (FTIR) and a 1-propenyl group (vinyl signals: one doublet and one doublet of quartets, indicating –CH=CH–CH3). The two –CH3 signals arise from the propenyl methyl and a methyl on the ester (either –COOCH3 or –OOCCH3). Summing the fragments: C6H4 (ring) + C3H5 (propenyl) + C2H3O2 (ester with methyl) = C11H12O2. This formula has 6 degrees of unsaturation (ring, ester carbonyl, vinyl), consistent with the data, and no –CH2 groups are present. Other options have incorrect hydrogen counts or would require –CH2 groups.

Answer: C
